name: Contemplation
momentumNotes: Action pauses so perception can deepen; seeing clearly is itself the movement.
theme: Contemplation stands still enough to see the whole. The wind moves over the earth, revealing patterns to those who do not hurry past them.
basicInterpretation: Before acting, look. A wider view may transform the question itself and show where your presence has influence.
reflectionPrompt: What can you understand only by becoming still enough to see?

reversed.theme: Flipped upside down, Contemplation becomes Hexagram 19, Approach. This other side brings in the atmosphere of arrival, encouragement, growth, asking how the situation may look from another threshold.
reversed.reflection: Let Approach widen the reading rather than replace it. Consider what another person, timing, or hidden part of you might see when the pattern is viewed from the far side.
reversed.applicationPrompt: Visualize your question from the far side, as if another person or your future self is looking back through Approach. Notice where arrival, encouragement, growth and a growing, moving movement reveal needs, timing, or motives that the first view may miss.

opposite.theme: The contrast to Contemplation is Hexagram 34, Great Power. Where the primary pattern emphasizes observation, perspective, reverence, this complementary field points toward strength, momentum, responsibility.
opposite.reflection: This is not the main movement of the reading, but it shows what balances or challenges it. It can also highlight hidden causes or contrasting forces at play. Notice where Great Power names the medicine, shadow, or unchosen path beside the situation.
opposite.applicationPrompt: Visualize Great Power as the contrasting color laid beside Contemplation. Ask what hidden cause, missing medicine, or opposing pressure is suggested by strength, momentum, responsibility, especially where the situation carries a powerful, abundant tone.
